stance_summary: Canada 5Y versus US 5Y is a dual-horizon historical tail, not a dip. The valuation anchor is the frozen CA-US 5Y spread at the 0.20th 1y / 6.95th 5y percentile after a 16bp 1m cheapening into a Fed hike that was already >90% priced. Convergence belongs in rates RV: short CA-US_5Y (Canada yields up versus US / US yields down versus Canada). Spot USDCAD is only moderately rich and is the inferior expression of the same relative gap.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Short CA-US_5Y at executable_marks.rates_rv.CA-US_5Y -124.00000000000003 (2026-09-17): fade the historically wide Canada-versus-US 5Y yield gap (economically long US 5Y duration versus short Canada 5Y duration).
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD at executable_marks.spot_fx.USDCAD 1.4010471204188482 (2026-09-18): CAD recovery if Canada rates re-rate higher versus the US.
expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing lives in the CA-US 5Y spread (1y percentile 0.20, 5y percentile 6.95, z_1y -2.03), not in USDCAD (1y percentile 74.0, 5y percentile 87.0, z_5y 0.99). Rates are cleaner, own the stretched object directly, and are preferred under the rates-first mandate. USDCAD is only a moderately rich analog and fights less of a documented tail.

trade.structure: Short the frozen CA-US 5Y sovereign yield spread (CA 5Y minus US 5Y). Book engine marks CA-US_5Y from market_state.rate_rv.CA-US_5Y.bps. Economically long US 5Y versus short Canada 5Y.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: as of 2026-09-17, CA-US_5Y is -124.00000000000003bp, 0.1984th percentile over 1y, 6.9456th over 5y, z_1y -2.0275, z_5y -1.3607, and it cheapened 16bp over 1m and 12bp over 5d (market_state.rate_rv.CA-US_5Y). Same-date CA-US_2Y is -140bp at the 3.77th 1y / 4.31st 5y percentile. US 5Y is 4.86 (99.60th 1y and 5y); Canada 5Y is 3.54 (97.82nd 1y, 81.78th 5y). The Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026 after futures entered that meeting with >90% hike odds; August CPI is cited as keeping a tightening bias. Canada August headline CPI held at 3.0% y/y with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%. Canada activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5 sit above US activity 49.92 and consumer 48.5; Canada labor 48.8 is softer (unemployment 6.4%, employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y) than US labor 50.2 (unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +162k). USDCAD spot 1.4010471204188482 is 74th 1y / 87th 5y. Paper books are empty $100m seeds; funded seats pay 5% ACT/365 on the full $100m whether deployed or not. Inference: this is a relative dislocation, not Canada cheap because it fell. Canada 5Y is only mid-to-high versus its own 5y history; US 5Y is the 99.6th percentile object, so the spread tail is a US-overshoot versus a still-firmer Canada activity/consumer pulse after a hike that was already in the price. Why convergence now: the Sep 16 FOMC print is known information, yet the 5Y spread made a new 1y tail into that event (-12bp / 5d, -16bp / 1m). That is the condition for using the historical distribution as more than a yardstick: stretch plus a completed, priced catalyst. The 5Y tenor owns the medium-term relative terminal better than 2Y around a just-printed FOMC and better than 10Y (CA-US_10Y 10.60th 5y versus 6.95th for 5Y). Unknown: packet has no REER/PPP, no BoC policy-rate field, no NZ yields, no options surface, and CME FX OI is unavailable. Energy is two-sided (BoC pass-through risk versus Saudi Oman workaround that reduced the oil-supply tail).
trade.mispricing: Valuation anchor is the CA-US 5Y spread versus its own 1y and 5y distributions, not the 1m yield change. At -124bp the spread is a 0.20th percentile 1y / 6.95th percentile 5y reading (z_1y -2.03) after a further 16bp 1m cheapening. That is historically too much Canada-versus-US cheapness once the priced Fed hike is stripped out. Peer check: CA-US_2Y is also a 4th-percentile 5y tail; USDCAD is not.
why_now: The 16 Sep 2026 25bp Fed hike was >90% priced before the meeting; that known event is in the US curve, while CA-US_5Y still sits at the 0.20th 1y percentile.
The same spread cheapened another 16bp over 1m and 12bp over 5d into that already-priced hike, which is the overshoot versus known information.

Canada activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5 remain above US 49.92 / 48.5, and BoC minutes flag energy pass-through, so the fundamental case for keeping Canada this cheap versus the US is not strengthening.
Empty $100m seed books still pay 5% ACT/365 on the full allocation while flat; this RV mark exists and is the dislocation that can clear the clock.

trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong, not merely early, if CA-US_5Y stays at or through the current 1y tail (0.20th percentile, z_1y -2.03, mark -124.00000000000003) because Canada core/labor remain clearly softer than the US after the next Canada CPI and employment prints and BoC energy pass-through does not appear, rather than because of a few days of timing noise. A further US-led selloff that leaves the relative tail intact also falsifies convergence.
catalysts: Post-hike fade in the US 5Y after the already-delivered 16 Sep 2026 25bp move.
BoC energy pass-through showing up in subsequent Canada headline/core CPI after the minutes flagged that risk.
Canada activity remaining firmer than the US without a matching 5Y re-rating.
principal_risks: Canada labor is already cooler (employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y, unemployment 6.4% versus US 4.1%), which can justify a structurally wider CA-US spread.
US core PCE ~3.0% 6m annualized versus Canada trim/median near 2% is a real inflation gap; some of the 124bp 5Y differential may be fair.
Further Fed tightening after August CPI can keep US 5Y at the 99.6th percentile and drive CA-US more negative.
Saudi Oman workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, which can remove the BoC pass-through catalyst.
Packet has no REER/PPP, no NZ yields, no CME FX OI, and no implied path beyond the already-printed hike.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: CA-US 5Y at -124bp is a 0.20th 1y / 6.95th 5y historical tail after a priced Fed hike, so Canada-versus-US cheapness should converge in rates RV rather than in only-moderately-rich USDCAD.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: The 16 Sep 2026 Fed hike was already >90% priced; remaining 1y-tail CA-US 5Y cheapness should start converging as that event premium fades and/or BoC energy pass-through re-rates Canada.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: CA-US_5Y holds or extends the 0.20th 1y tail because Canada core and labor stay clearly softer than the US, not because of short timing noise.

paper_capital.funding_hurdle_rationale: Funded seats pay 5.00% simple ACT/365 on the full $100m every day (~$13,699/day, $5m/year) even when flat; paper books are empty seeds so the vig is already running. Short CA-US_5Y at the frozen mark -124.00000000000003. Book rates_rv P&L is -sign*(mark-entry)/100*notional, so a 10bp spread normalization on $20m is about $2.0m versus about $1.23m of vig over 90 days; the 16bp 1m cheapening already in the packet is the same order of magnitude. Outright long AU or US duration cannot clear that clock under the book's /100 yield convention. Carry of long US 5Y versus short CA 5Y is the ~124bp yield pickup, which supports rather than fights the RV. Being flat still pays the 5% and forfeits that edge.
